Open weights let you own the model.

They don't give you the person who keeps it running.

Budget for both.
Open weights are the only honest benchmark left. Everything behind an API is an unannounced mixture of routing heuristics, prompt caches, and silent quantizations pretending to be a single model.

The biggest mistake in AI is building things you don't understand. Before calling yourself an AI builder, learn the language behind the technology. LLMs, tokens, context windows, prompts, inference, latency and hallucinations are the fundamentals.

Want to build smarter

Open weights are more than a cheaper way to run AI.

They give developers control over deployment, customization, experimentation and infrastructure choices.

I think model openness will become an important part of technical sovereignty.

#OpenSourceAI #AIEngineering

The No.2 AI on Artificial Analysis's cyber security index is one anyone can download. Open-weights Kimi K3.1 Pro scored 64%, just 5 points behind a closed model you need special access to use. Risk, or a security guard every small business can have?

Frontier models feel too expensive per token. Open weights are good value. I judge both by cost per finished task now, and the expensive model often lands the work cheaper because it makes fewer wrong turns and gets the shape right the first time.

New open weights from Italy: Translated's Lara Mini Base. 7.2B-total / 0.6B-active MoE, trained from scratch on 6T tokens in 45 languages (all 24 EU ones), 128K ctx. ~14.6 GB bf16 weights. Base model only, no chat tuning; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, gated on HF.

A legged humanoid learned a warehouse plank-picking task from half an hour of examples and got it right 15 times out of 15, @runwayml says.

It runs Praxis-1, the robot model the AI video company just released as open weights for anyone to use.

Gartner says open weights cover about 90% of agentic workflow steps at a fifth to a twentieth of frontier cost.

That 90% counts steps, and steps are the cheap part. Budget for the last 10% landing on a frontier model, then measure your own mix rather than theirs.

The honest bill for owning your model: GPUs that are expensive and scarce, open weights that trail the frontier, and security that stops being someone else's problem. Still worth it: the gap closes and cost per query drops. @rbenzaquen and I run that math at @shefaventures.
